question: Should denylist join the existing layered `tools.exec` plus `exec-approvals.json` policy and override `security=full`, `ask=off`, and durable trust on every execution host?
rationale: Correct implementation does not settle whether this stronger, persisted cross-host security contract is the intended product policy; the exec owner must accept its compatibility and operator impact.

options.title: Accept layered deny-over-allow
options.body: Approve both existing policy layers with strict fail-closed validation, union semantics, one-shot approvals, and final-commit revocation across every host.

options.title: Limit to approvals storage
options.body: Expose denylist only through `exec-approvals.json` to reduce the new public config and protocol surface.

options.title: Reject the feature direction
options.body: Keep current exec modes if maintainers do not want permissive full/off workflows interrupted by a STOP list.

recommendation.title: Accept layered deny-over-allow
recommendation.body: Approve both existing policy layers with strict fail-closed validation, union semantics, one-shot approvals, and final-commit revocation across every host.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current-main history in the affected authorization paths and is explicitly named in the discussion for the security-contract decision.
